title: rate shock IRR sensitivity
_comment: Hand-computed ground truth for the rate shock case. The bullet facility is priced at base rate plus spread; the shocked case reprices the same facility 200 bp higher with everything else unchanged. The warrant valuation factor 0.15 is a stated assumption, not a market quote. Inputs are pinned test vectors, exempt from band validation. Expected values are already quantized at their storage or metric boundary with ROUND_HALF_UP, exactly as the engine will publish them.
arithmetic: step 1: base all_in_rate = base_rate 4.0000 + spread 3.0000 = 7.0000, scale 4 percent_annual, exact sum, no rounding needed.

step 2: rate_shock_bp 200 bp = 2.0000 percent; shocked base_rate = base_rate 4.0000 + 2.0000 = 6.0000, shocked all_in_rate = 6.0000 + spread 3.0000 = 9.0000, scale 4 percent_annual, exact sums, no rounding needed.

step 3: close 2026-01-05 is Monday, a business day; payment date k = roll_forward(add_months(close, k)) for k = 1 to 5; day of month 5 is preserved because every target month has at least day 5, so no clamping occurs in F6; business days are Monday to Friday with no holiday table.
step 4: payment date 1 = add_months(close 2026-01-05, 1) = 2026-02-05 is Thursday, a business day, no roll. Period 1 spans (2026-01-05, 2026-02-05], days_between = 31, ACT/365 year fraction = 31/365.
step 5: payment date 2 = add_months(close 2026-01-05, 2) = 2026-03-05 is Thursday, a business day, no roll. Period 2 spans (2026-02-05, 2026-03-05], days_between = 28, ACT/365 year fraction = 28/365.

step 6: payment date 3 = add_months(close 2026-01-05, 3) = 2026-04-05 is Sunday, roll forward to Monday 2026-04-06. Period 3 spans (2026-03-05, 2026-04-06], days_between = 32, ACT/365 year fraction = 32/365.
step 7: payment date 4 = add_months(close 2026-01-05, 4) = 2026-05-05 is Tuesday, a business day, no roll. Period 4 spans (2026-04-06, 2026-05-05], days_between = 29, ACT/365 year fraction = 29/365.
step 8: payment date 5 = add_months(close 2026-01-05, 5) = 2026-06-05 is Friday, a business day, no roll. Period 5 spans (2026-05-05, 2026-06-05], days_between = 31, ACT/365 year fraction = 31/365.

step 9: the five payment dates 2026-02-05, 2026-03-05, 2026-04-06, 2026-05-05, 2026-06-05 are strictly increasing; days from close to the final payment = 31 + 28 + 32 + 29 + 31 = 151, ACT/365 year fraction close to final payment = 151/365.

step 10: base period 1 interest = all_in_rate 7.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.07 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 31/365 = 594,520.5479452054794520547945 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 594,521 cents.

step 11: base period 2 interest = all_in_rate 7.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.07 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 28/365 = 536,986.3013698630136986301370 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 536,986 cents.

step 12: base period 3 interest = all_in_rate 7.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.07 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 32/365 = 613,698.6301369863013698630137 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 613,699 cents.

step 13: base period 4 interest = all_in_rate 7.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.07 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 29/365 = 556,164.3835616438356164383562 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 556,164 cents.

step 14: base period 5 interest = all_in_rate 7.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.07 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 31/365 = 594,520.5479452054794520547945 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 594,521 cents.

step 15: shocked period 1 interest = shocked all_in_rate 9.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.09 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 31/365 = 764,383.5616438356164383561644 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 764,384 cents.

step 16: shocked period 2 interest = shocked all_in_rate 9.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.09 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 28/365 = 690,410.9589041095890410958904 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 690,411 cents.

step 17: shocked period 3 interest = shocked all_in_rate 9.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.09 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 32/365 = 789,041.0958904109589041095890 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 789,041 cents.

step 18: shocked period 4 interest = shocked all_in_rate 9.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.09 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 29/365 = 715,068.4931506849315068493151 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 715,068 cents.

step 19: shocked period 5 interest = shocked all_in_rate 9.0000 percent_annual / 100 = 0.09 x facility 100,000,000 cents x 31/365 = 764,383.5616438356164383561644 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 764,384 cents.

step 20: bullet structure: principal = 0 cents in periods 1 to 4 and 100,000,000 cents in period 5 in both schedules; opening balance period 1 = facility 100,000,000 cents; opening balance period t equals the prior closing balance; closing balance = opening minus principal gives 100,000,000 cents in periods 1 to 4 and 0 cents in period 5; total_principal = 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 100,000,000 = 100,000,000 cents, exact integer sum; the base and shocked schedules share identical balances and principal because only the rate changes.
step 21: total_interest base = 594,521 + 536,986 + 613,699 + 556,164 + 594,521 = 2,895,891 cents, exact integer sum of the quantized rows, no further rounding.
step 22: total_interest shocked = 764,384 + 690,411 + 789,041 + 715,068 + 764,384 = 3,723,288 cents, exact integer sum of the quantized rows, no further rounding.

step 23: closing_fee = closing_fee_pct 1.00 percent x facility 100,000,000 cents = 1,000,000 cents = 10,000.00 USD, exact product, no rounding needed; lender cash flow at close = fee 1,000,000 minus facility 100,000,000 = -99,000,000 cents, dated 2026-01-05.

step 24: warrant_value = warrant_coverage_pct 2.00 percent / 100 = 0.02 x facility 100,000,000 cents x warrant_valuation_factor 0.15 = 300,000.0000 cents at MONEY_CONTEXT prec 28, single quantize to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 300,000 cents = 3,000.00 USD, cash flow dated at the final payment date 2026-06-05.

step 25: lender cash flows base: at close 2026-01-05 the lender collects fee 1,000,000 and funds facility 100,000,000, cash flow -99,000,000 cents; at payment dates 1 to 4 the lender receives interest 594,521, 536,986, 613,699, 556,164 cents; at payment date 5 the lender receives interest 594,521 plus principal 100,000,000 plus warrant 300,000 = 100,894,521 cents.
step 26: IRR year fractions from close, ACT/365 on cumulative day counts 31, 59, 91, 120, 151: 31/365, 59/365, 91/365, 120/365, 151/365.

step 27: base IRR solves sum_i CF_i x (1 + r)^(-yf_i) = 0 over the base lender cash flows; Decimal bisection with bracket [-0.99, 10.00], midpoint (lo + hi) / 2, sign decisions only, terminated when hi minus lo fell below 0.000001 after 24 iterations, final r = 0.106818601191043853759765625; published base_irr_percent = r x 100 = 10.68186011910438537597656250 quantize to scale 4 percent_annual with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 10.6819.

step 28: NPV bracket for base_irr_percent 10.6819: at r = (10.6819 minus 0.0001) / 100 = 0.106818 NPV = 11.443079 cents, positive; at r = (10.6819 plus 0.0001) / 100 = 0.106820 NPV = -61.712835 cents, negative; the sign change proves the root lies within the 0.0001 percent tolerance of the published value.

step 29: shocked IRR solves the same equation over the shocked lender cash flows; Decimal bisection with bracket [-0.99, 10.00], midpoint (lo + hi) / 2, sign decisions only, terminated when hi minus lo fell below 0.000001 after 24 iterations, final r = 0.129079991877079010009765625; published shocked_irr_percent = r x 100 = 12.90799918770790100097656250 quantize to scale 4 percent_annual with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 12.9080.

step 30: NPV bracket for shocked_irr_percent 12.9080: at r = (12.9080 minus 0.0001) / 100 = 0.129079 NPV = 32.605627 cents, positive; at r = (12.9080 plus 0.0001) / 100 = 0.129081 NPV = -38.873104 cents, negative; the sign change proves the root lies within the 0.0001 percent tolerance of the published value.
step 31: irr_delta_bp = (shocked_irr_percent 12.9080 minus base_irr_percent 10.6819) x 100 = 222.6100 bp, quantize to scale 1 with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 222.6 bp.

step 32: sensitivity_per_100bp_irr_bp = irr_delta_bp 222.6 / 2 = 111.3 bp because the rate shock is exactly 200 bp, so the per 100 bp sensitivity is the delta divided by 2, quantize to scale 1 with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 111.3 bp.

step 33: moic = (total_interest 2,895,891 + total_principal 100,000,000 + warrant_value 300,000) / facility 100,000,000 = 1.03195891, quantize to scale 2 with ROUND_HALF_UP once = 1.03, closing fee excluded from the numerator, computed from the base flows.

step 34: warrant_coverage_pct 2.00 is greater than 0.00, so the warrant is granted and warrant_value publishes as 300000 usd_minor_units; the shock changes no balance, principal, fee, or warrant value, only interest and therefore the lender cash flows and the IRR.

base_rate.source: fixture pinned rate, not a Valet observation
